result.summary: Invitation tokens now expire after one week (7 days, the same period as project transfer tokens). The full suite ran: 1762 passed and 1 failed. The failure is a date-dependent test that is not related to this change (details below). All tokens are issued through one helper, `generate_invitation_token()` in `taiga/projects/services/invitations.py`, which returns the token and its expiration date together; `set_invitation_token()` applies both to a membership. The issuers that now use it: API create, bulk create, project import and the `sample_data` command. A token is valid only while `token_expires_at` is in the future. Expired tokens and old tokens with no expiration date behave like unknown tokens: getting the invitation by token, logging in and private registration all return 404, and the invitation is not accepted. Resending an invitation gives it a new token and a new expiration date, so the old link stops working. `token` and `token_expires_at` are now read-only in `MembershipValidator`, so API clients can no longer set them. Both membership factories create tokens valid for one week. The failing test is `tests/unit/test_due_date_serializers.py::test_due_date_status[due_date4-False-due_soon]`. It computes `timezone.now().date()` when pytest collects the tests. The 14-minute run crossed midnight UTC, so at run time that date was already yesterday and the serializer returned 'past_due'. That test and that serializer use no code I touched. I wanted to confirm this by running the test on the clean tree, but the git stash command was denied. Nothing was committed.

changes.summary: Added INVITATION_TOKEN_LIFETIME (7 days), generate_invitation_token(), set_invitation_token() and resend_invitation(), which rotates the token; get_membership_by_token only matches tokens with token_expires_at in the future (legacy NULL dates are rejected).
pre_save issues tokens through set_invitation_token; resend_invitation rotates the token; InvitationViewSet.get_queryset hides expired and legacy tokens (404).
Bulk invitations use generate_invitation_token; removed unused uuid import.
Imported memberships use set_invitation_token, which overwrites any expiration date in the dump; removed unused uuid import.
token and token_expires_at are read-only in MembershipValidator, so clients cannot set them.
MembershipFactory and InvitationFactory set token_expires_at to now + 7 days.
Tests for login and private registration with valid, expired and legacy invitation tokens.
Tests for the helper, API create, bulk create, client-supplied token ignored, resend rotation, and get invitation by valid, expired or legacy token.
Test that import gives invitations a fresh token valid for 7 days.

acceptance.criterion: Every issuer sets the token and its expiration date together through one shared helper
acceptance.evidence: API create (pre_save), bulk create (get_members_from_bulk), import (_store_membership) and sample_data all use generate_invitation_token or set_invitation_token. Tests cover API create, bulk create and import.

acceptance.criterion: Expired and legacy tokens are rejected everywhere
acceptance.evidence: Parametrized tests (expired and None) for GET /invitations/<token>, login with invitation_token and private registration return 404, the invitation is not accepted and no user is created: all pass.

acceptance.criterion: Resending gives a new valid token
acceptance.evidence: test_api_resend_invitation_rotates_token passes: a new token valid for 7 days, the email contains the new token, the old token returns 404 and the new one returns 200.
New tests in test_auth.py, test_memberships.py and test_importer_api.py pass.

Full `pytest tests` run: 1762 passed, 1 failed. The failure is test_due_date_status[due_date4-False-due_soon]. Its parameter `timezone.now().date()` is computed when pytest collects the tests, and the run crossed midnight UTC, so the serializer returned past_due. The test and the serializer use no code I touched. I could not confirm this on the clean tree because the git stash command was denied. No model changed, so no migration was needed.

human_needed.question: Is it OK that `token` and `token_expires_at` are now read-only for API clients?
human_needed.why: Before, a client could set its own token, and that token would have no expiration date. A frontend that writes these fields would be affected.

human_needed.question: Should existing pending invitations get a migration that sets an expiration date, instead of being treated as expired?
human_needed.why: As the task asks, all invitations that are pending today stop working until an admin resends them.
